A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoVE/ROVE study. All 41 pages of v3 and 42 pages of v4, including appendices, support comparison; relocated proofs and experimental plots can be matched.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D report original regression experiments, stochastic-optimization simulations, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: Section 3 and Appendix F retain original empirical results and add regression comparisons against bagging.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same subsampling, candidate retrieval, voting, and optional data-splitting procedures. Adaptive threshold selection is unchanged between v3 Appendix D.3 and v4 Appendix F.3.

E1.justification: V4 Figure 2 adds synthetic MLP evaluations with Pareto noise shapes 1.5 and 1.1 alongside the existing 2.1 condition. The six real datasets and stochastic-optimization tasks remain covered.

E2.justification: V4 adds bagging, implemented as subagging by averaging predictions from four-hidden-layer MLPs, as an evaluated comparator in Figure 2. V3 discusses bagging but does not report this comparison.

E3.justification: The new bagging comparison matches subsampling and ensemble budgets and uses k2=max(30,n/1000), B2=1000; existing regression defaults remain k2=max(30,n/200), B2=200. The reported runtime comparison contracts from n=2^7–2^15 to 2^7–2^11 and no longer separates execution modes.

E4.justification: New Figure 2 tests sensitivity of the bagging comparison to noise-tail heaviness. The explicit sequential-versus-parallel timing comparison disappears. Existing hyperparameter and robustness analyses remain, including the LP tail-heaviness analysis moved from v3 Figure 4a to v4 Figure 18.

E5.justification: Both retain 200 independent synthetic datasets, 100 real-dataset permutations, and 95% confidence intervals for mean-performance plots. The added bagging plots follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Figure 2 shows bagging achieving lower MSE at Pareto shape 2.1, while ROVE and ROVEs perform better at shape 1.1. V3 Figure 3f's portfolio-tail results disappear, and the runtime comparison loses larger-sample and separately labeled execution-mode results. Most existing results are retained.

T1.justification: V4 changes introductory Equation (2) from a polynomial upper bound to a lower bound. It adds the LP Example 1.1, Corollary 2.2 and its proof, and Appendix E's regression assumptions, Theorem E.2, and lower-bound/ensemble-bound derivations. The original general bounds remain as Theorems C.7 and C.11.

C1.justification: The central learner-agnostic polynomial-to-exponential tail-improvement claim remains. V4 removes the introduction's additional claim that average-case regret also improves exponentially for discrete problems.

C2.justification: V4 adds a rationale for focusing on regression based on cross-entropy's logarithm and explains the inference-cost benefit of selecting one model. It removes the conclusion's general warning about increased subsampling bias and suitability for low-bias applications, although Figure 10 retains its specific high-bias explanation.

D1.justification: V4 documents the bagging implementation and settings but removes the runtime caption's eight-core specification and the explanation that maximization objectives are negated for plotting. The anonymous code link disappears; the public GitHub link and MLP architecture details remain.

R1.justification: V4 trims the tree-boosting discussion and removes the XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Vapnik references. It adds an inference-cost distinction from conventional ensembles. The learning-to-optimize review is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The introduction and theoretical narrative are extensively rewritten around mode estimation. Detailed main-text bounds move to Appendix C, technical lemma proofs are separated into Appendix D, and experimental material moves to Appendix F, including the previously main-text configuration summary.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column main text and references, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and algorithms. It adds the three-panel bagging figure, reorganizes the stochastic-program panels, redraws the runtime comparison, removes the portfolio-tail panel, and relocates the LP sensitivity plot.

improvement.justification: The worked theoretical examples and Figure 2's direct bagging comparison make the central argument more concrete and better contextualized, including reporting cases where bagging wins. These support a modest net improvement, tempered by removal of the general bias caveat, portfolio-tail evidence, and runtime execution details.
